messages.author: 5eafd1ef6d900b85
messages.subject: knitr and data.table
parts:
I'm not sure if this is a knitr, evaluate or data.table issue

I am trying to use data.table within a knitr document and I keep getting evaluation errors such as 
'error: undefined columns selected'

The errors and output differ depending on whether the document is cached or not.

The r code runs when not being put through knitr.

I have reformatted the data.table introductory vignette to be used in with knitr + spin as a (rather long)
reproducible example.

The two files are here
https://gist.github.com/2927672

dt-vig.r is the file with cache = T
dt-vig-cache-F.r is the same file, but with cache = F

I run these files by calling

system('Rscript do-dt.r')
system('Rscript do-dt-cache-F.r')
where 

do-dt.r contains

library(knitr)
spin('dt-vig.r')

and

do-dt-cache-F.r contains

library(knitr)
spin('dt-vig-cache-F.r')

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr and data.table
parts:
It is likely to be a bug of data.table. In the past, knitr has
revealed similar bugs in ggplot2, plyr and np. The problem is that the
package author(s) did not think carefully about the environments in
which the code is evaluated. Here is a simple test that can be used to
confirm if it is a bug of the package:

eval(quote{
# put the relevant piece of code here
}, envir = new.env())

If this shows an error of some objects not found, it indicates a bug
of that package.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: RE: [knitr] knitr and data.table
parts:
I have a smaller example

#' small example
#'
#' `r opts_chunk$set(cache = T, env)`
#'
#+ setup, cache = F
library(data.table)
DT = data.table(x=c("b","b","b","a","a"),v=rnorm(5))
setkey(DT,x)
#'
#'
#' with cache = F
#+ DT-false, cache = F
DT["b", mult = "first"]
DT["b" ]
#'
#' with cache = T
#+ DT-true, cache = T
DT["b", mult = "first"]
DT["b" ]
#' what does this mean?

This gives the two errors.

If I run

eval(parse( text = '
library(data.table)
DT = data.table(x=c("b","b","b","a","a"),v=rnorm(5))
setkey(DT,x)
## @knitr DT-false
DT["b", mult = "first"]
DT["b" ]
## @knitr DT-true
DT["b", mult = "first"]
DT["b" ]
'), env= new.env())

within R there is no error

But, if I run this in knitr

I get

Error: undefined columns selected
